description.narrative: The purpose of this proposal is to strengthen tiger conservation in the Banke-Bardia tiger conservation landscape of western Terai in Nepal. This will be done by: assessing the status of the newly recolonizing tiger and prey base population of Banke Nationial Park (BaNP); and strengthening public engagements and law enforcement in and around BaNP for tiger conservation. Specifically, this will be done by: 1) holding a project orientation workshop for community leaders, the project team and park officials; 2) carrying out a winter camera trap tiger monitoring survey and two replications of a transect prey base monitoring survey; 3) carrying out district level interaction workshops for government agencies, political parties, conservation organizations and civil society members in Banke, Salyan and Dang districts; 4) training (20) local youths as nature guides and engaging them in tourism; 5) preparing a tiger conservation booklet (1,000 copies) in the local language focused on the ethnic communities in the buffer zone and using them during the conservation education sessions; 6) conducting 20 interactive conservation education awareness sessions in schools and 20 similar events in local communities of the buffer zone; 7) supporting at least 40 tiger affected and vulnerable families of 15 VDCs to adopt viable alternative livelihood options; 8) forming five community based anti-poaching units (CBAPU) in each sector of the BaNP buffer zone; 9) training 30 CBAPU members from each CBAPU (over five one sessions) in CBAPU operation, overview of wildlife crime in Nepal, CBAPU efforts to reduce wildlife crime and the code of conduct for CBAPU members; 10) conducting a three day exposure trip to Bardia National Park for 40 CBAPU members to observe the activities of that parks CBAPU; 11) supporting the salary of one full time program officer who will facilitate implementation of the projects public engagement related activities; 12) providing orientation training to the Ba
